key_insight: A large fraction of token-to-token attention scores in video diffusion transformers are consistently negligible and often repeatable across queries, so the model can safely skip those attention computations with careful calibration to retain output quality.
problem_solved: Text-to-video diffusion models produce high-quality results but run slowly because spatiotemporal attention across many tokens is computationally expensive. The paper reduces wasted attention computation to speed up generation.
method: Analyze attention matrices to identify token-to-token connections that consistently yield near-zero scores and find repeating sparsity patterns across queries.
Construct calibrated sparse attention masks (e.g., per-layer/head thresholds or lightweight gating) that skip low-impact attention computations while controlling for fidelity loss.
Integrate the sparse attention mechanism into transformer backbones of text-to-video diffusion models to reduce runtime without degrading perceptual/video quality.
impact: Practitioners can generate videos faster and cheaper by avoiding redundant attention work, enabling higher throughput, lower latency, or larger-resolution video synthesis with the same hardware. The technique is applicable to other large spatiotemporal transformers beyond text-to-video.

paper_title: Accelerating Text-to-Video Generation with Calibrated Sparse Attention
